channel.title: Relay blog
channel.description: Notes on how the Relay harness works: orchestration by Michael, isolated Git worktrees, the Claude Code and Codex CLI provider contract, and the local-first safety boundary.

item.title: Worktree isolation, and what it refuses to do
item.description: Every task gets its own relay/orchestrator-* branch and managed worktree, so your checked-out branch stays untouched until you accept a diff yourself.

item.title: Inside the orchestrator: how Michael plans a run
item.description: Michael plans in a read-only mode, returns a validated one-to-four task plan, and falls back to a deterministic plan rather than stranding the run.

item.title: Introducing Relay: many coding agents, one orchestrator
item.description: Relay is a local-first desktop harness that drives the Claude Code and Codex CLI clients you already installed, against a Git project you already have on disk.
